**suggestion (bug_risk):** Avoid using raw SYS_gettid syscall for better portability.

This helper (and the similar usage in the PM4 IB dumper) relies on `syscall(SYS_gettid)`, which is Linux-specific and not guaranteed to exist or behave consistently on all Mesa targets or libcs. static pid_t
```c
a0_gettid(void)
{
#ifdef __linux__

#else

   return (pid_t)(uintptr_t)pthread_self();
#endif
}
```

nodes.body: The SemWait narrowing in scan_read() only registers a pending TEX dependency when *v is NULL (i.e., on the first read of that temp component in the block). If multiple instructions in the block read the same carried-over TEX result, only the first encountered reader gets TexReadCount>0; the scheduler is free to emit a different reader first, which would then execute without SemWait and may observe incomplete TEX results. Consider registering add_tex_reader() for every reader that reads a PendingTEX-written temp component (even when *v already exists but has no Writer in this block), so any consumer cannot be scheduled ahead of the wait.

ntr_try_fold_srcmod_to_ssa() can cause fabs/fneg to emit no instruction even when the chased ALU dest has fsat folded (dst.Saturate == true via nir_legacy_chase_alu_dest). In that case the original code applied saturation via the MOV/MAX destination, but the new fold path drops the saturate modifier entirely (and the separate fsat op is skipped), changing results. Ensure the fold is disabled when saturation is required (e.g., if the chased dest has fsat set / dst.Saturate is true), or otherwise preserve saturation semantics.

Selects[] was expanded to a fixed-size array of 8, but can_use_presub_data_add_select() still increments SelectCount and writes into Selects[SelectCount++] without any bounds check. Since the number of selects depends on opcode sources and presub expansion, add a guard/assert against SelectCount >= ARRAY_SIZE(Selects) to avoid potential buffer overflow if constraints change.

nodes.body:
**issue (bug_risk):** Scalar ALU helpers ignore destination saturation, which can change shader results

These helpers emit per-channel scalar instructions but drop the `fsat`/dest saturate from the original NIR ALU op. For ops like `frcp`, `frsq`, and `fexp2`, NIR may require saturation, yet RC instructions are always emitted with `RC_SATURATE_NONE`, unlike the TGSI path. This can change shader outputs. Please pass a `bool saturate` (or `SaturateMode`) into `nrc_emit_scalar` and set `inst->U.I.SaturateMode` accordingly when emitting scalar instructions.

**issue (bug_risk):** Unlowered flrp causes a hard error and fallback, but the error is only logged to stderr

In this path, you set `c->error = true`, which propagates to `compiler->Error`, but never populate `ErrorMsg`. As a result, `r300_translate_fragment_shader()` sees `compiler.Base.Error` while `compiler.Base.ErrorMsg` is NULL, making `shader->error = strdup(compiler.Base.ErrorMsg)` undefined. Please route this through the existing RC error reporting (e.g., `rc_error(compiler, ...)` or explicitly set `compiler->ErrorMsg`) so the caller gets a valid message and does not dereference NULL. Longer term, either guarantee `flrp` is lowered before this pass or implement the MAD-based expansion instead of hard-failing here.

**issue (bug_risk):** UBO handling ignores block/binding layout and assumes constant index==vec4_offset

This path (1) assumes `src[0]` (binding) and `src[1]` (offset) are compile-time constants via `nir_src_as_uint`, (2) ignores the binding and uses `vec4_offset` as the constant index, and (3) does not implement the `RC_CONSTANT_EXTERNAL` layout used by the TGSI path. That means UBO loads will likely read the wrong constant slot, and any non-constant offset will hit assertions. Please either mirror the TGSI `RC_CONSTANT_EXTERNAL` allocation/mapping (including per-block offsets), or explicitly reject non-constant UBO loads and emit `compiler->ErrorMsg` so the TGSI fallback is used until proper mapping is implemented.

**issue (bug_risk):** System-value inputs (frag_coord, front_face, point_coord, VS system IDs) all use hardcoded input slot 0

These intrinsics all hardcode `SrcReg[0].Index = 0` with TODOs, effectively aliasing distinct system values onto the same RC input index. That’s inconsistent with the existing TGSI/ureg path (`rc_transform_fragment_wpos`, `rc_transform_fragment_face`, VS system-value lowering) and is likely to return wrong values or cause cross-talk between system inputs. Please either (a) pass through the actual input indices produced by the NIR→RC lowering (mirroring the TGSI path), or (b) gate/disable this direct NIR path when any of these intrinsics are present until proper index mapping is implemented.

This file uses assert() and fprintf(stderr, ...) but doesn't include <assert.h> or <stdio.h>, which can cause build failures depending on include order. Add the required standard headers (or switch to rc_error/DBG helpers) so the file compiles consistently.

This issue also appears on line 935 of the same file.

nrc_emit_scalar() forces SrcReg[0].Swizzle to xxxx for every destination channel. For vector rcp/rsq/ex2/lg2/sin/cos/pow this will compute all enabled dst components from src0.x instead of the matching src component (taking swizzles into account). Emit per-component scalar ops using the corresponding source channel (similar to nir_to_rc.c:ntr_emit_scalar).

store_output currently shifts the destination writemask by `component` but does not shift the source swizzle accordingly. This will write the wrong values whenever `component != 0` (e.g., writing src.x to out.y). Adjust the source swizzle based on `frac` and the final writemask, like nir_to_rc.c:ntr_emit_store_output does.

load_output ignores nir_intrinsic_component() and always uses RC_SWIZZLE_XYZW. For partial/offset loads this will read incorrect components. Apply the same component shifting logic as load_input (and avoid swizzling undefined channels when the dest writemask excludes them, as done in nir_to_rc.c:ntr_emit_load_output).

load_frag_coord is hardcoded to read RC_FILE_INPUT index 0. This will be wrong unless WPOS happens to be assigned to input 0, and it will also break rc_transform_fragment_wpos() which expects the actual WPOS input index from shader->inputs.wpos. The direct emitter needs to derive and use the real WPOS slot (or lower load_frag_coord to load_input with the correct base before RC emission).

This issue also appears in the following locations of the same file:
- line 649
- line 663

r300_nir_fill_shader_info() iterates NIR variables 1:1 but doesn't account for multi-slot variables (arrays/matrices), and it doesn't apply the same varying-slot fixups used by nir_to_rc (see ntr_fixup_varying_slots()) before calling tgsi_get_gl_varying_semantic(..., needs_texcoord_semantic=true). As a result, TEX0..TEX7 inputs can become TGSI_SEMANTIC_TEXCOORD (which r300_shader_read_fs_inputs() doesn't handle), and num_inputs/semantic arrays can disagree with the actual slot layout.

For FS outputs, tgsi_get_gl_frag_result_semantic() needs dual-source adjustment (var->data.index > 0) and multi-slot handling; otherwise output semantic indices can be wrong (e.g., COLOR0 vs COLOR1 for dual-source) and num_outputs can be undercounted for arrays. Consider mirroring the logic in nir_to_tgsi_info.c for semantic derivation.

r300_nir_to_rc_direct() only sets compiler->Error=1 on failure but doesn't populate compiler->ErrorMsg. Callers (including r300_fs.c) strdup(ErrorMsg) on error, so this can crash or yield a useless error. Use rc_error() (or otherwise set ErrorMsg) when flagging c->error, and consider skipping rc_calculate_inputs_outputs() when c->error is set.

External constant placeholders are preallocated using `s->num_uniforms`, but the RC emission uses absolute constant indices (e.g., vec4_offset from load_ubo) that must match the constant space layout expected by later compilation and by r300 constant uploads. This risks reading the wrong constants or missing slots entirely. Instead, derive the required external constant count/mapping from the lowered NIR (or mirror the TGSI path’s `file_max[TGSI_FILE_CONSTANT] + 1` allocation strategy).

The PIPE_SHADER_IR_NIR branch no longer calls nir_to_rc() (which runs extensive lowering such as nir_lower_io, nir_convert_from_ssa/nir_lower_vec_to_regs, tex lowering, varying-slot fixups, shadow lowering, etc.). r300_nir_to_rc_direct() and r300_nir_fill_shader_info() both assume those passes have run (and even UNREACHABLE on remaining vec ops). Add a shared lowering entrypoint (factored out of compiler/nir_to_rc.c) and run it here (likely on a clone) before fill_shader_info/direct emission, or keep the existing nir_to_rc lowering sequence for the NIR path.

On direct NIR->RC translation error, this code assumes compiler.Base.ErrorMsg is populated and calls strdup() on it. r300_nir_to_rc_direct currently only flips compiler->Error without guaranteeing ErrorMsg, which can lead to a crash (strdup(NULL)) or a misleading empty error. Ensure the direct emitter sets ErrorMsg (e.g., via rc_error) before returning an error.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve per-component swizzles in scalar ALU emission**

This helper forces scalar ops to always read `.x` (`nrc_scalar_swizzle(0)`) for every written destination channel, so vector forms of `frcp/frsq/fexp2/flog2/fsin/fcos/fpow` compute all components from `src.x` instead of from each channel. The previous path emitted one scalar op per channel with that channel's swizzle, so shaders that apply these ops to `vec2/vec3/vec4` inputs will now produce incorrect results.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include UBO binding in constant slot addressing**

UBO loads currently index constants only by `vec4_offset`, which aliases all bindings onto the same constant range and returns wrong data whenever a shader accesses binding > 0 (or multiple UBOs). The old TGSI path encoded both binding and offset (including indirect forms), so this direct path regresses uniform fetch correctness for multi-UBO shaders.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resolve fragment system-value slots instead of hardcoding 0**

Reading `load_frag_coord/load_front_face/load_point_coord` from input slot 0 is not valid in general: slot assignment depends on declared FS inputs and rasterizer wiring. This causes these intrinsics to read unrelated varyings whenever slot 0 is not the required semantic, producing incorrect fragment coordinates/front-face/point-coord behavior in affected shaders.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Run required NIR lowering before direct RC translation**

The new NIR path calls `r300_nir_to_rc_direct` on `state.ir.nir` directly, but this emitter explicitly depends on the lowering sequence previously done by `nir_to_rc()` (IO lowering, legacy trivialization, texture/op lowering, register lowering, etc.). Bypassing that pipeline means ordinary shaders can still contain intrinsics/opcodes this backend marks as unsupported, causing compile failures or incorrect code generation where the previous path succeeded.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Guard direct-path error reporting against NULL ErrorMsg**

On direct translation failures, this branch unconditionally does `strdup(compiler.Base.ErrorMsg)`, but `r300_nir_to_rc_direct` sets `compiler->Error` without guaranteeing `ErrorMsg` is populated. If a failure comes from one of its local `c->error = true` paths, `ErrorMsg` can be NULL and this call can crash instead of gracefully falling back to the dummy shader.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Add intrinsic base when indexing UBO constant loads**

The direct UBO load path uses only `src[1] / 16` for the constant index and ignores `nir_intrinsic_base(instr)`, while the previous path added the intrinsic base before applying the dynamic/static offset. Any load with a non-zero intrinsic base will fetch from the wrong constant slot, returning incorrect uniform values.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Respect barycentric mode in load_interpolated_input**

This case emits a plain MOV from `RC_FILE_INPUT` and ignores the barycentric source (`instr->src[0]`) entirely, so centroid/at-sample/at-offset interpolation requests are dropped. Shaders using `interpolateAtCentroid`, `interpolateAtSample`, or `interpolateAtOffset` will read values at the wrong interpolation point compared with the prior path that emitted explicit interpolation ops for these modes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Populate FS input semantics per slot, not per variable**

The replacement shader-info fill iterates input variables and increments `ni` once per variable, but TGSI-style input metadata is per register slot (including multi-slot arrays/matrices). Multi-slot inputs therefore get collapsed into a single semantic entry, which can misalign semantic-to-register mapping used by FS input allocation and lead to incorrect or missing varying assignment.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply load_input offset source when reading FS inputs**

NIR `load_input` uses a base+offset form, but this path always reads `RC_FILE_INPUT[base]` and never applies `instr->src[0]`. Any shader that indexes fragment inputs (for example arrays lowered to `load_input` with non-zero/dynamic offsets) will read the wrong varying register compared to the previous TGSI path, which handled this offset via indirect input addressing.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Check UBO sources are constant before nir_src_as_uint**

This code unconditionally calls `nir_src_as_uint` for both UBO binding and offset, but that helper requires constant sources; non-constant sources can hit assertions or null dereferences in this path. The prior translator explicitly supported indirect UBO indices/offsets, so shaders with dynamic UBO access can now crash compilation instead of being translated.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**suggestion (bug_risk):** Treating any failure to read `install.dat` as a prefix mismatch may obscure the root cause.

```suggestion
	        meson setup $(SETUP_ARGS) --prefix=$(PREFIX) $(BUILDDIR) $(TOPSRC); \
	        new_dat_prefix=$$(python3 -c "import pickle; print(getattr(pickle.load(open(\"$(BUILDDIR)/meson-private/install.dat\",\"rb\")), \"prefix\", \"\"))" 2>/dev/null); \
	        new_dat_status="$$?"; \
	        if [ "$$new_dat_status" -ne 0 ]; then \
	            echo "[install] FAIL: cannot read $(BUILDDIR)/meson-private/install.dat after reconfigure; refusing to install" >&2; \
	            exit 1; \
	        fi; \
	        if [ "$$new_dat_prefix" != "$(PREFIX)" ]; then \

```

`r300_pack_float24` doesn’t validate that the biased exponent fits in the intended 7-bit field (bits 22:16). For sufficiently small magnitudes, the biased exponent can go negative and (after the cast) turn into a very large unsigned value. Consider range-checking the biased exponent (and rejecting unsupported inputs) so the utility always emits a valid float24 encoding.

nodes.body: `Block::kcache_rollback()` now clears `m_readport_exhaustion_failed`, but there are call sites that take a KCACHE snapshot, call `try_schedule_vec_candidate(...)`, and then unconditionally call `kcache_rollback(snapshot)` on failure (e.g. the PV/PS seeker in `schedule_alu_to_group_vec`). In the `add_vec_instructions` rejection path, `try_schedule_vec_candidate` sets `mark_readport_exhaustion_failed()` after its own rollback, but the caller’s rollback will clear the flag again, preventing `schedule_alu()` from seeing it and splitting the clause. Consider either (a) removing the redundant caller rollback when `try_schedule_vec_candidate` already restored KCACHE, or (b) splitting rollback into “restore KCACHE state” vs “clear failure flags”, so the failure signal survives until the outer scheduling loop consumes it.

`readport_exhaustion_failed()` is used as a general “vec candidate rejected for local-to-group reasons” signal (see the add_vec_instructions failure path and the log text "readport or local"), but `schedule_alu()` reports this as "readport exhaustion" and the flag name implies only readport exhaustion. This makes the stderr message (and any diagnostics keyed off the flag) potentially misleading. Consider renaming the flag/message to something generic (e.g. local vec constraint failure) or, if you want to keep the readport name, only set it when the rejection is specifically due to readport exhaustion and use a separate flag for other local constraints.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve readport-failure flag across speculative rollback**

`kcache_rollback` now clears `m_readport_exhaustion_failed`, but speculative callers still invoke rollback after a failed candidate probe (e.g. the PV/PS seeker path in `schedule_alu_to_group_vec` calls `kcache_rollback(kc_save)` on failure). In the case where `try_schedule_vec_candidate` sets the new flag and returns false, that outer rollback erases the signal before `schedule_alu` can clause-split on it, so the scheduler can fall back to the NOP path instead of splitting and still emit the malformed bundle this change is trying to prevent.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restrict readport-failure flag to true readport exhaustion**

This marks `readport_exhaustion_failed` on every `add_vec_instructions` rejection, but that function also rejects for non-readport reasons (e.g. PARAM bank mismatch, LDS co-issue rules, destination topology/pinning constraints). Treating all of those as readport exhaustion forces the clause-split/AR-bailout path in `schedule_alu`, so shaders can be failed or split even when the failure was unrelated to KCACHE readport pressure.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clear stale readport-failure state after successful packing**

The new `readport_exhaustion_failed` state is consulted as a hard split trigger, but unlike the existing KCACHE flags it is never cleared by successful KCACHE reservations. After one transient rejection sets the flag, later unrelated no-progress iterations can still enter the split branch through this sticky state, bypassing the normal NOP-conflict recovery and potentially tripping the AR-in-use compile failure path unnecessarily.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep LDS-group scheduling off KCACHE-failure assert path**

Adding `readport_exhaustion_failed()` to this branch routes every flagged vec rejection into logic that asserts `!m_current_block->lds_group_active()`. Because the new flag is set for generic `add_vec_instructions` rejections (including LDS-related co-issue/topology cases), an in-progress LDS group can now hit this branch and trigger the debug assert even though no KCACHE reservation/preflight failure occurred.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**suggestion (bug_risk):** Clarify why the new clause is explicitly started as Block::alu rather than mirroring the previous Block::unknown.

Elsewhere in this function, `start_new_block` is called with `Block::unknown` for partial‑group/cleanup, but this new clause split uses `Block::alu`. If downstream logic infers clause type from the block kind, this difference could change scheduling behaviour. If the intent is to always start a typed ALU clause here, that’s fine, but consider either reusing the current block type or adding a brief comment explaining why we normalize to `Block::alu` in this case.

```suggestion
   /* Start a fresh clause with an unknown type, matching other
    * partial-group/cleanup clause splits in this function. The clause
    * kind will be inferred when instructions are added to the block. */
   if (success &&
       m_current_block->readport_exhaustion_failed() &&
       !m_current_block->lds_group_active() &&
       m_current_block->expected_ar_uses() == 0) {
      start_new_block(out_blocks, Block::unknown);
   }
```

✅ Addressed in 4cd781389fef25c03987a0004ed0faa248f8ddd7: A detailed comment has been added above this block explaining the partial-group clause split and explicitly describing that a fresh ALU clause is opened here, clarifying the intent behind using Block::alu instead of Block::unknown.

The new clause-split is keyed off `m_current_block->readport_exhaustion_failed()`, but that flag is currently set on *any* `AluGroup::add_vec_instructions()` rejection (see `try_schedule_vec_candidate`, which marks it whenever `add_vec_instructions` returns false). Since `add_vec_instructions()` can fail for reasons other than Evergreen readport exhaustion (e.g., PARAM source mismatch, LDS/topology/pinning constraints), this change can start new ALU clauses even when the rejection wasn't a per-clause readport exhaustion, potentially increasing CF/ALU clause count.

Consider tightening the signal so it is only raised for actual readport exhaustion (e.g., propagate a specific failure reason out of `try_readport` / `AluReadportReservation::last_error()`), or introduce a separate flag for the broader “local group constraint” failures and keep this clause-split guarded by the readport-specific condition.

This block comment is very location-/chronology-focused (e.g., references to specific line ranges and positional wording like “above/here/next invocation”). AGENTS.md asks for source comments to be mechanism-focused and avoid deictic/chronology breadcrumbs; it’d be more durable to describe the invariant (partial group commit + readport exhaustion requires a clause split to reset per-clause accounting) without referencing specific line numbers or relative code positions.

nodes.body: r300vk_CreateRenderPass writes pCreateInfo->attachmentCount entries into rp->attachments (sized PIPE_MAX_COLOR_BUFS + 1) and sp->colorAttachmentCount entries into rp->color_attachment_refs (sized PIPE_MAX_COLOR_BUFS) without any bounds checks. If either count exceeds these fixed limits this will overflow the struct and corrupt memory. Please validate counts and return an error (or clamp + track) before copying.

r300vk_CreateFramebuffer memcpy()s attachmentCount VkImageView handles into fb->attachments, but fb->attachments is a fixed array of PIPE_MAX_COLOR_BUFS + 1. If attachmentCount is larger, this will overflow and corrupt memory. Please validate attachmentCount against the array size and return an error when exceeded.

CmdBeginRenderPass resolves rp->color_attachment_refs[0] to an index and uses it directly to index fb->attachments without validating it. This is unsafe if the attachment reference is VK_ATTACHMENT_UNUSED (~0u) or otherwise out of range of fb->attachment_count, and will lead to OOB reads and crashes. Also, load_op is taken from rp->attachments[0] rather than from the resolved attachment index, so non-zero attachment indices will use the wrong loadOp; and if load_op is CLEAR but clearValueCount==0, clear_color is left uninitialized and later read during replay.

CmdBindVertexBuffers ignores firstBinding and records bound buffers starting at slot 0. This produces incorrect bindings whenever firstBinding != 0 (and also makes it impossible to satisfy Gallium's requirement that set_vertex_buffers count == max vertex_buffer_index + 1). Please record the start slot and populate the correct indices (including leaving gaps NULL as needed) so replay can call set_vertex_buffers with a correctly-sized array.

r300vk_CreateDevice unconditionally uses pCreateInfo->pQueueCreateInfos[0] to initialize the queue without validating that queueCreateInfoCount > 0. If an application passes zero queues (invalid but possible without validation layers), this will read out of bounds. Please add a defensive check and return VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED (or a more appropriate error) if no queues are provided.

r300vk_MapMemory assumes mem->resource can be mapped with pipe_context::buffer_map and uses u_box_1d with mem->resource->width0. However BindImageMemory2 assigns a PIPE_TEXTURE_2D resource to mem->resource; mapping a texture with buffer_map (and unmapping with buffer_unmap) is incorrect and can crash or corrupt memory. MapMemory/UnmapMemory/FreeMemory need to select buffer_map/buffer_unmap vs texture_map/texture_unmap based on resource->target, and compute the mapping box appropriately for textures.

BindBufferMemory2/BindImageMemory2 ignore VkBind*MemoryInfo::memoryOffset and simply alias mem->resource to the buffer/image resource. If memoryOffset is non-zero, the bound address will be wrong and MapMemory(offset) won't match what the app expects. Please either (a) validate that memoryOffset==0 and return an error for unsupported offsets, or (b) track the offset in the binding and apply it consistently in MapMemory and other operations.

r300vk_replay_gpu binds vertex elements state in R300VK_CMD_BIND_PIPELINE, but set_vertex_buffers may have been replayed earlier (depending on original Vulkan call order). This violates the Gallium contract that frontends MUST call set_vertex_buffers after bind_vertex_elements_state and before the next draw (pipe/p_context.h:417-421), and can lead to incorrect vertex fetch or driver assertions. Please ensure replay always re-issues set_vertex_buffers after binding vertex elements (e.g., by caching the last bound VB state in cmd buffer and re-binding it in the pipeline bind path).

R300VK_CMD_BEGIN_RENDER_PASS replay unconditionally dereferences e->begin_rp.color_image and hardcodes fb.nr_cbufs=1. However CmdBeginRenderPass can record color_image == NULL (no color attachment, VK_ATTACHMENT_UNUSED, or invalid indices), which would crash here. Please handle the no-color-attachment case safely (nr_cbufs=0 and skip clear) and validate the recorded attachment pointer before dereferencing.

Scissor replay casts VkRect2D offset.x/y to unsigned. Vulkan allows negative scissor offsets; casting will wrap to a huge value and produce an invalid scissor box. Please clamp offsets at 0 and ensure maxx/maxy are computed safely within unsigned bounds.

CPU readback maps dst with dst_size = width*height*4, but then uses row_pitch derived from bufferRowLength. When bufferRowLength > imageExtent.width, the loop writes up to (height-1)*row_pitch + width*4 bytes, which can exceed the mapped range and cause OOB writes. Please compute the required mapped size from row_pitch (and bufferImageHeight/layer stride if supported) and validate bufferOffset + required_size against dst->width0 before memcpy.

r300vk_queue_driver_submit ignores vk_queue_submit::waits and ::signals (wait_count/signal_count) entirely. This breaks Vulkan queue submission semantics (semaphores/fences won't be waited/signaled), which can cause data races and incorrect results across queues or between CPU and GPU. Please integrate vk_sync waits/signals handling (similar to other drivers' driver_submit implementations) or explicitly reject submits with waits/signals until supported.

r300vk_cmd_append grows the command entry array via realloc/free, bypassing the Vulkan command pool allocator (pool->alloc) and any VkAllocationCallbacks behavior expected by the runtime. This can lead to inconsistent allocation tracking and ignores VK_COMMAND_BUFFER_RESET_RELEASE_RESOURCES_BIT semantics. Please allocate/grow cmd->entries using the pool allocator (or util_dynarray with vk_* alloc helpers) and honor the reset flags by releasing memory when requested.

r300vk_compile_shader treats every non-vertex stage as fragment (creates FS state in the else branch) and the error message only distinguishes vertex vs fragment. If a pipeline includes any other stage (e.g., geometry), this will compile/bind the shader into the wrong stage slot. Please validate that stage_info->stage is one of the supported stages and return a clear error for unsupported stages.

If info->pInputAssemblyState is NULL, pl->topology is left uninitialized but later used during draw replay (vk_topology_to_mesa(cmd->bound_pipeline->topology)). Please either require pInputAssemblyState and validate it, or initialize topology to a safe default to avoid undefined behavior.

The comment says the build is guarded so it "fails clearly if only one is set" (r300vk-gallium-backend vs with_gallium_r300), but the Meson logic only conditionally adds Gallium-backed sources; it doesn't emit an error if the option is enabled without the r300 Gallium driver. Consider either updating the comment to reflect the actual behavior or adding an explicit error() when r300vk-gallium-backend is true but with_gallium_r300 is false (or vice versa).

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clamp render-pass attachment count to fixed storage**

`r300vk_render_pass` stores attachments in a fixed array (`PIPE_MAX_COLOR_BUFS + 1`), but this loop copies `pCreateInfo->attachmentCount` entries without any bound check. A render pass with more attachments than that fixed capacity will write past `rp->attachments`, corrupting heap/stack state during `vkCreateRenderPass`; the driver should reject unsupported counts or allocate storage dynamically.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bound-check framebuffer attachment memcpy**

`fb->attachments` is a fixed-size array, but `memcpy` uses `pCreateInfo->attachmentCount` as the byte count source with no capacity check. If the render pass/framebuffer uses more attachments than the local array size, this overflows `fb` and can crash or corrupt later command recording/submission; reject oversized counts or store attachments dynamically.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Size readback mapping from row pitch, not image width**

The destination map size is computed as `width * height * 4`, but the copy loop writes rows at `row_pitch` bytes where `row_pitch` can be larger when `bufferRowLength` is set. In that valid Vulkan case, the loop writes past the mapped range and corrupts memory during `CmdCopyImageToBuffer2`; the mapped byte size must include the effective row pitch (and related layout fields) used by the copy.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Snapshot draw topology instead of using final bound pipeline**

Draw replay derives `info.mode` from `cmd->bound_pipeline`, which is the command buffer’s mutable “last bound” pipeline, not the pipeline bound at each draw. If a command buffer binds different graphics pipelines before different draws, all draws can be replayed with the final pipeline’s topology, producing incorrect primitive assembly.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Honor firstBinding when recording vertex buffer binds**

`vkCmdBindVertexBuffers` includes `firstBinding`, but this implementation computes `count` only from `bindingCount` and later replays with `set_vertex_buffers(..., count, ...)` from slot 0. Calls that update non-zero binding slots or partial ranges will overwrite the wrong bindings and feed incorrect vertex data to draws.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve firstInstance in draw replay**

`firstInstance` from `vkCmdDraw` is dropped during replay: only `instance_count` is set on `pipe_draw_info`, so `start_instance` remains zero. Instanced draws that rely on non-zero base instance will compute `InstanceIndex`/instance-addressed fetches incorrectly.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply memoryOffset when binding memory to resources**

`BindBufferMemory2` ignores `pBindInfos[i].memoryOffset` and just aliases the whole buffer resource into the memory object. Valid suballocated bindings (non-zero offset) will map/access the wrong address range, breaking applications that place multiple resources in one allocation; the bind path needs to preserve and apply the offset semantics.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Return vk_command_buffer_begin failures**

`r300vk_BeginCommandBuffer` always returns `VK_SUCCESS` and discards the result of `vk_command_buffer_begin`. If begin fails (e.g., internal allocation/state transition failure), callers receive a false success and continue recording against an errored command buffer, which can cascade into harder-to-debug failures later.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Respect queue wait/signal sync objects in submit path**

This submit implementation replays command buffers and returns success, but never processes `submit->wait_count`/`submit->waits` or `submit->signal_count`/`submit->signals`. As a result, inter-queue and WSI synchronization contracts are broken: work may start before required waits and downstream waiters may never observe signals.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle VK_ATTACHMENT_UNUSED before framebuffer lookup**

`VkAttachmentReference::attachment` is allowed to be `VK_ATTACHMENT_UNUSED`, but this code unconditionally uses `color_attachment_refs[0]` as an index into `fb->attachments`. When that value is `VK_ATTACHMENT_UNUSED`, the huge sentinel index causes out-of-bounds access during command recording.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply image memoryOffset when binding image memory**

`BindImageMemory2` also drops `pBindInfos[i].memoryOffset` and aliases the full image resource directly. For valid suballocated image bindings, mapped or copied data is addressed as if the image started at offset 0, producing incorrect memory aliasing and data corruption.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject unsupported image dimensions/layers/samples**

Image creation hardcodes a 2D, single-layer, single-mip, single-sample Gallium resource (`depth0=1`, `array_size=1`, `last_level=0`, `nr_samples=1`) regardless of the requested `VkImageCreateInfo`. Requests for array images, mipmapped images, or multisampled images can return success but back a different resource shape than requested, leading to later out-of-bounds accesses or wrong rendering behavior.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
